691: /**
692:  * Interface exposed by a Gatekeeper instance implementing a specific resource binding on a
693:  * specific Gadget.
694:  *
695:  * The Gatekeeper executes as a Durable Object Facet, where it is a child of the Overseer. This
696:  * interface is exposed to the Overseer, not directly to the Gadget.
697:  */
698: export interface Gatekeeper<Session> extends DurableObject {
699:   /**
700:    * Get more info on the specific resource without actually granting access. This information is
701:    * to be presented to the user in the UI, before the user actually confirms they want to grant
702:    * access.
703:    */
704:   describe(): Promise<ResourceDescription>;
705: 
706:   /**
707:    * Returns the a subset of the type definitions returned by
708:    * GatekeeperVendor.getTypeScriptTypes(), specifically covering types used by this Gatekeeper.
709:    * This allows the agent to be provided with only types relevant to them rather than the entire
710:    * API space of the vendor, which may support many kinds of resources.
711:    */
712:   getTypeScriptTypes(): Promise<string>;
713: 
714:   /**
715:    * Catalog of action kinds this gatekeeper MAY auto-apply without per-action review, for
716:    * pre-approval UIs that must list them before any action has been submitted. Each entry is the
717:    * {tag, label} an action of that kind carries on its ActionDescription.actionKind. This is the
718:    * *potential* set; the per-action `autoApprovable` verdict is still the binding gate at apply
719:    * time. Gatekeepers with no auto-approvable actions return [].
720:    */
721:   getAutoApprovableActions(): Promise<ActionKind[]>;
722: 
723:   /**
724:    * Get the capability representing this resource's RPC interface which will be provided to the
725:    * Gadget.
726:    *
727:    * Every operation performed through this session must be submitted to the approval queue.
728:    * Observations (read-only operations) must be authorized before data is returned to the caller.
729:    * Side-effecting actions must not actually be performed until they are approved.
730:    *
731:    * It is suggested that the gatekeeper "simulate" actions that have not been approved yet, that
732:    * is, the `Session` interface should reflect the state of the resource as if all actions had
733:    * been applied. This allows the Gadget to keep working, potentially queuing up additional
734:    * dependent actions. That said, there is no strict requirement that a gatekeeper does such
735:    * simulation -- it is really up to the gatekeeper author to decide what is appropriate for the
736:    * particular API.
737:    */
738:   startSession(approvalQueue: RpcStub<ApprovalQueue>): Promise<Session>;
739: 
740:   /**
741:    * Bounded, user-specific metadata the agent uses to discover entries reachable through this
742:    * gatekeeper's session, without paging the full session API. Implemented only by gatekeepers
743:    * whose session benefits from a discovery index (e.g. an agent singleton like the Context
744:    * Library); most gatekeepers omit it. Catalog access is an observation, so the implementation
745:    * must authorize it via `authorizer.authorizeObservation()` before returning metadata. Returns
746:    * null when there is no catalog. Return the entries the agent most needs first and pass them
747:    * through `boundAgentCatalog()`, since both that clamp and the Workshop's drop from the tail.
748:    */
749:   getAgentCatalog?(
750:     authorizer: RpcStub<ObservationAuthorizer>,
751:   ): Promise<AgentCatalog | null>;
752: 
753:   /**
754:    * Informs the gatekeeper that a new user is being added to the Gadget with the potential to see
755:    * all data that was read from this Gatekeeper in the past.
756:    *
757:    * `id` is a unique, stable, but opaque string chosen by the overseer to identify this user in
758:    * the context of this gadget.
759:    *
760:    * The gatekeeper must verify that the given user is allowed to directly observe everything that
761:    * has been observed through this gatekeeper in the past. If this is not the case, addObserver()
762:    * must throw an exception.
763:    *
764:    * If this returns without throwing, the Gatekeeper must remember that this user is now an
765:    * observer. If any future observation must be hidden from this observer, then the
766:    * `ObservationDescription` must include the `excludeObservers` property to indicate who is not
767:    * permitted to see the observation.
768:    *
769:    * `addObserver()` may be called again with the same user ID. If so, the gatekeeper should re-run
770:    * the same verifications it would have done if the user were newly-added. The overseer may run
771:    * this periodically to check if the user's access to the resource may have been revoked.
772:    *
773:    * For most gatekeepers, addObserver() should simply check that the user is allowed to read the
774:    * target resource in general -- there's no actual need to check against a log of past
775:    * observations. For gatekeepers that provide broad access to a user's resources, though, it may
776:    * be unlikely that any other user could possibly have access to everything the gatekeeper provides.
777:    * In these cases, logging what was actually observed makes things more useful.
778:    *
779:    * For example, imagine a gatekeeper that grants access to a user's email inbox. Full access to
780:    * an inbox is extremely personal and usually no other user can possibly be permitted such broad
781:    * access. However, if the Gadget itself carefully reads only emails addressed to a particular
782:    * mailing list, then it is OK to reveal those observations to any member of the mailing list.
783:    * The gatekeeper should ideally permit observers who are mailing list members.
784:    */
785:   addObserver(id: string, user: Fetcher<GatekeeperUserVerifier>): Promise<void>;
786: 
787:   /**
788:    * Notifies the gatekeeper that it can stop tracking the given observer, who was previously
789:    * added using `addObserver()`. The gatekeeper no longer needs to verify whether each observation
790:    * is safe for this observer.
791:    *
792:    * This method must be idempotent: If the gatekeeper is unaware that this user was ever added, it
793:    * should just ignore the call rather than throw.
794:    */
795:   removeObserver(id: string): Promise<void>;
796: 
797:   /** Returns the provider for describe().hasSlashCommands, if supported. */
798:   getSlashCommandProvider?(): Promise<SlashCommandProvider>;
799: 
800:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
801:   // Callbacks invoked by the overseer to apply (or reject) actions that were previously queued
802:   // for approval via the ApprovalQueue.
803:   //
804:   // Each action is identified by a sequential integer action ID, assigned by the gatekeeper when
805:   // it submits the action for approval. The action ID is passed back to these methods so the
806:   // gatekeeper can look up the action details in its own storage.
807: 
808:   /**
809:    * Action was approved. This call should apply the action (or schedule it to be applied).
810:    *
811:    * If this throws an exception, the user will be informed that the action failed and given the
812:    * opportunity to retry or discard.
813:    *
814:    * Depending on policy conditions, an action may be approved and applied automatically. However,
815:    * the gatekeeper is nevertheless expected to submit all actions for approval; there is no mode
816:    * in which it's OK to skip the check.
817:    */
818:   applyAction(action: number): Promise<void>;
819: 
820:   /**
821:    * Indicates that an action was rejected by the user. The gatekeeper should clean up any
822:    * associated storage.
823:    *
824:    * If the returned `restart` flag is true, rejecting this action requires restarting the Gadget.
825:    * This is sometimes needed by gatekeepers that simulate actions as if they had been approved --
826:    * the session may be in a state that is difficult to roll back without confusing the Gadget.
827:    * The Overseer will take care of the restart, possibly after rejecting other actions.
828:    */
829:   rejectAction(action: number): Promise<void | {restart?: boolean}>;
830: 
831:   /**
832:    * Attempts to revert an action that was already applied.
833:    *
834:    * Gatekeepers are not required to implement this. If unimplemented, the user will be instructed
835:    * that they need to perform the revert manually based on the action description. High-quality
836:    * gatekeepers should almost always implement this, though.
837:    *
838:    * If the returned `message` is non-null, it is Markdown to be displayed to the user. This may
839:    * be used, for example:
840:    * - To give the user additional instructions on how to complete the revert, if not all of it
841:    *   could be done automatically.
842:    * - To explain to the user why a revert is not possible, e.g. if other stacked modifications
843:    *   have been made on top which must be reverted first. (`canRetry` may be true in this case.)
844:    *
845:    * `canRetry` should be true if the revert failed (for a reason described in `message`), but
846:    * it could make sense to retry later. In this case the UI will continue to give the user the
847:    * option to revert.
848:    *
849:    * `restart` has the same meaning as for `rejectAction()`.
850:    */
851:   revertAction(action: number):
852:       Promise<void | {message?: string, canRetry?: boolean, restart?: boolean}>;
853: }
854: 
855: export interface ObservationAuthorizer extends RpcTarget {
856:   /**
857:    * Check whether the gadget should be permitted to make an observation (that is, to read some
858:    * data from an external service). The gatekeeper calls this on every read operation, and must
859:    * wait for the response before returning anything to the gadget. The method will return normally
860:    * if the operation is permitted, or throw an exception if not; the exception should propagate
861:    * through to the gadget.
862:    *
863:    * In many cases, the gatekeeper should actually call this *after* fetching the data from the
864:    * remote service, so that the description can include details about the actual data. As long
865:    * as the operation is strictly read-only, and the call is made before actually returning any
866:    * data to the gadget, this is OK.
867:    */
868:   authorizeObservation(description: ObservationDescription): Promise<void>;
869: }

876:   /** Optional skill name for the display badge. Commands that do not represent skills omit it. */

879:   /**
880:    * Final text to insert into chat as if the user had sent it. The provider owns all formatting and

882:    */
883:   message?: string;

887: export type SlashCommandDescriptor = {
888:   /** Opaque ID local to this provider. Passed back to invoke(). */
889:   id: string;
890: 
891:   /** Name shown after `/` in the picker. */
892:   name: string;
893: 
894:   /** Short description shown in the picker. */
895:   description: string;
896: 
897:   /** Optional label for the underlying resource (e.g. a collection path), used when names collide. */
898:   resourceLabel?: string;

901: /**
902:  * Optional API for a Gatekeeper that offers slash commands.
903:  *
904:  * list() returns non-sensitive picker metadata. Before invoke() returns expansion text derived from
905:  * protected data, it must use `authorizer` to authorize and audit the read. The provider cannot
906:  * submit actions or bind hooks.
907:  */
908: export interface SlashCommandProvider extends RpcTarget {
909:   /**
910:    * Complete catalog of commands offered by this provider. Providers should keep this reasonably
911:    * small.
912:    */
913:   list(): Promise<SlashCommandDescriptor[]>;
914: 
915:   /**
916:    * Runs the command identified by `id`, which must be an ID previously returned by list().
917:    * `args` is the unparsed natural-language text following the command. The provider owns all
918:    * expansion semantics and may return final text to insert as an ordinary user message.
919:    * `authorizer` remains authorization and audit only. The provider must reject unknown IDs.
920:    */
921:   invoke(
922:     id: string,
923:     args: string,
924:     authorizer: RpcStub<ObservationAuthorizer>,
925:   ): Promise<SlashCommandResult>;

928: /**
929:  * Used by a gatekeeper to request an action that has side effects (is not read-only). Any such
930:  * action may be subject to human-in-the-loop approval and audit logging. Whether or not review is
931:  * actually required, the gatekeeper must still submit all actions and wait for apply() to be
932:  * called before applying them.
933:  */
934: export interface ApprovalQueue extends ObservationAuthorizer {
935:   // TODO: Method to indicate that the gadget tried to perform an action that the gatekeeper itself
936:   //   hasn't been authorized to do (e.g. the user hasn't authorized the right OAuth scopes). The
937:   //   system should direct the user to the right UI to authorize the action.
938: 
939:   /**
940:    * Submit an action for approval.
941:    *
942:    * Unlike `authorizeObservation()`, `submitAction()` is fully asynchronous. It returns
943:    * immediately (that is, the returned Promise resolves quickly), but the action may not actually
944:    * be carried out until much later. It's intended that the user might not approve actions until
945:    * hours or days later, but this shouldn't cause any problems.
946:    *
947:    * `action` is a sequential integer action ID assigned by the gatekeeper. It will be passed back
948:    * to the Gatekeeper's applyAction() or rejectAction() when the action is later approved or
949:    * rejected.
950:    *
951:    * `description` describes the action in a way that can direct UI representation and policy
952:    * enforcement details.
953:    *
954:    * TODO: It would be nice if we can link this with the output gate so that if the submission
955:    *   does not complete, any SQL writes performed just before submit() are rolled back...
956:    */
957:   submitAction(action: number, description: ActionDescription): Promise<void>;
958: 
959:   /**
960:    * Notifies the overseer that the gadget (or an agent) has requested to register a persistent
961:    * callback hook.
962:    *
963:    * `callback` is the stub received from the Gadget, which is intended to be called whenever some
964:    * event occurs. Although `callback` is always a persistent stub (see below), the gatekeeper
965:    * should NOT try to store it on its own; it should always pass it to `bindHook` for the overseer
966:    * to store. Why? Because the callback needs to be bound to a particular gatekeeper *session*.
967:    * At the time you are calling `bindHook()`, the callback is tied to the session that is tied
968:    * to the `ApprovalQueue`. But that session will end at some point, after which the callback stub
969:    * you received is revoked. When you call HookInitiator.startHook() later on, that actually
970:    * initiates a *new* session (returning a new `ApprovalQueue`), and the callback returned then
971:    * is tied to that session instead.
972:    *
973:    * `controller` is an object implemented by the gatekeeper which allows the overseer to enable
974:    * or disable the hook.
975:    *
976:    * The hook is not immediately enabled, as the user may need to approve it first. If and when
977:    * the user has approved, the overseer will call controller.enable() to request that the the
978:    * gatekeeper begin delivering hook events. If the user never approves, no call will ever be
979:    * made. Therefore, the gatekeeper should avoid storing any state until the hook is enabled.
980:    * Typically, the `HookController` implementation should capture all information it needs to
981:    * register the hook into `props` so that it doesn't need to store anything elsewhere.
982:    *
983:    * In a typical implementation, the gatekeeper may expose an API to the gadget like:
984:    *
985:    *     onSomeEvent(callback: RpcStub<SomeInterface>)
986:    *
987:    * Where `SomeInterface` can be either an RpcTarget-derived interface, or a function type, but
988:    * either way the stub must be a persistent stub (see below). The gadget could call `onSomeEvent`
989:    * directly, but more commonly an agent will call it in a one-off `executeCode` tool call, since
990:    * this is usually one-time setup, not something that happens programmatically. The
991:    * implementation of `onSomeEvent` constructs a `HookController` implementation whose `props`
992:    * specify the details of the event to be hooked, then calls `bindHook()` to register the hook.

216:   async #openGadgetInternal(id: string, shareKey?: string,
217:                             configureObservers?: RpcStub<ObserverConfigCallback>)
218:       : Promise<NativeRpcStub<Overseer>> {
219:     let userId = this.#userId.toString();
220:     let profileId = this.#userId.name!;
221:     let overseerId;
222:     try {
223:       overseerId = this.overseers.idFromString(id);
224:     } catch {
225:       throw createOpenGadgetError(OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceNotFound);
226:     }
227:     let overseer = this.overseers.get(overseerId);
228: 
229:     // HACK: Detect loss of the connection to the DO by:
230:     // - Pass a callback to overseer.open() which it should call when the session is disposed.
231:     // - Detect if the callback itself is disposed before being called, suggesting the connection
232:     //   was lost.
233:     // If the connection is lost, we abort this I/O context, which kills the WebSocket from the
234:     // client, forcing it to engage its reconnect logic, which should recover.
235:     // TODO: Implement onRpcBroken() in the built-in RPC system, matching Cap'n Web, and use that
236:     //   instead.
237:     // TODO: Consider how to reconnect to one DO without resetting the whole WebSocket. Probably
238:     //   needs new code on the client side. However, typically a client only ever opens one
239:     //   gadget at a time (since each tab is a separate client), so it's probably fine for now.
240:     let closed = false;
241:     let started = false;
242:     let notifyClosed = () => {
243:       closed = true;
244:     };
245:     (notifyClosed as any)[Symbol.dispose] = () => {
246:       if (started && !closed) {
247:         // this.ctx.abort() would be nicer here, but it is still marked experimental in the
248:         // workers runtime.
249:         this.abortSession(new Error(`lost connection to workspace DO (gadget ${id})`));
250:       }
251:     }
252: 
253:     let result;
254:     try {
255:       result = await overseer.open(userId, profileId, notifyClosed, shareKey, configureObservers);
256:     } catch (err) {
257:       // A denial proves this user's listing for the workspace is stale: revocation tries to drop it
258:       // (refreshAffectedCollaboratorListings), but that push is best-effort. Only catches entries
259:       // they click; others stay frozen at revocation, as a disconnected collaborator gets no pushes.
260:       if (getOpenGadgetErrorCode(err) === OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceAccessDenied) {
261:         await this.#user.forgetSharedGadget(id);
262:       }
263:       throw err;
264:     }
265:     started = true;
266:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
267:       event_name: "gadget_opened",
268:       user_id: userId,
269:       gadget_id: id,
270:       source: shareKey ? "share_key" : "direct",
271:     });
272:     return result;
273:   }

433:   async newGadgetFromBlueprint(
434:     blueprintId: string,
435:     bindings: Record<string, BlueprintBindingAssignment>
436:   ): Promise<RpcStub<Overseer>> {
437:     // 1. Read blueprint from KV.
438:     let kvRecord = await readBlueprintKvRecord(this.env, blueprintId);
439:     if (!kvRecord) throw new Error("Blueprint not found.");
440: 
441:     // 2. Read gzip-compressed Yjs doc from R2 and decompress.
442:     let codeBytes = await readBlueprintContent(this.env, blueprintId, kvRecord.metadata.version);
443:     if (!codeBytes) throw new Error("Blueprint content not found in R2.");
444: 
445:     // 3. Create new Overseer DO (same as newGadget()).
446:     let id = this.overseers.newUniqueId().toString();
447:     await this.#user.newGadget(id, kvRecord.metadata.title);
448:     let overseerResult = await this.#openGadgetInternal(id);
449: 
450:     // 4. Initialize from blueprint code.
451:     let overseerDo = this.overseers.get(this.overseers.idFromString(id));
452:     await overseerDo.initializeFromBlueprint(codeBytes, kvRecord.metadata.title,
453:         deploymentOutputForBlueprint(await readAdminConfig(this.env), blueprintId,
454:             sanitizeBlueprintOutput(kvRecord.metadata.output)));
455: 
456:     // 5. Create gatekeepers from assignments and bind them into the workspace's (only) gadget.
457:     let metadata = await overseerResult.getMetadata();
458:     using gadget = await overseerResult.getGadget(metadata.defaultGadgetId!);
459: 
460:     // Defensively put blueprint bindings into a map (not a raw object) until we've had a chance to
461:     // validate the names.
462:     let blueprintBindings = new Map(Object.entries(kvRecord.metadata.bindings));
463:     let gadgetId = metadata.defaultGadgetId!;
464: 
465:     // Create gatekeepers in two phases: first every non-spawner binding (binding the
466:     // non-spawnerOnly ones into the gadget, and recording each created gatekeeper's id by
467:     // binding name), then the agent spawners, whose configs reference the phase-one results
468:     // symbolically (see SpawnerEnvTarget).
469:     let createdIds = new Map<string, WorkpieceId>();
470:     let gkPromises: Promise<void>[] = [];
471: 
472:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
473:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
474:       if (!blueprintBinding) {
475:         throw new Error(`Unknown binding name: ${bindingName}`);
476:       }
477: 
478:       gkPromises.push((async () => {
479:         let gk;
480:         if (assignment.type === "gatekeeper") {
481:           gk = await overseerResult.newGatekeeper(assignment.accountId, assignment.resourceUrl);
482:           if (!gk) {
483:             throw new Error(`Failed to create gatekeeper for binding "${bindingName}".`);
484:           }
485:         } else if (assignment.type === "aiModel") {
486:           gk = await overseerResult.newAiModelGatekeeper(assignment.modelId);
487:         } else {
488:           return;  // agent spawners are created in phase two
489:         }
490:         try {
491:           let id = await gk.getId();
492:           createdIds.set(bindingName, id);
493:           // A spawnerOnly binding exists purely to feed some spawner's env; it is not bound
494:           // into the gadget itself.
495:           if (!blueprintBinding.spawnerOnly) {
496:             await gadget.bind(bindingName, id);
497:           }
498:         } finally {
499:           gk[Symbol.dispose]();
500:         }
501:       })());
502:     }
503: 
504:     await Promise.all(gkPromises);
505: 
506:     // Phase two: agent spawners, with the full AgentSpawnerConfig reconstructed -- displayName
507:     // from the binding's title, modelId from the assignment, and env resolved against the
508:     // phase-one gatekeepers and the new gadget.
509:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
510:       if (assignment.type !== "agentSpawner") continue;
511:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
512:       if (blueprintBinding?.type !== "agentSpawner") {
513:         throw new Error(`Binding "${bindingName}" type mismatch.`);
514:       }
515: 
516:       let env: Record<string, WorkpieceId> = {};
517:       for (let [envName, target] of Object.entries(blueprintBinding.env)) {
518:         if (target.type === "gadget") {
519:           env[envName] = gadgetId;
520:         } else {
521:           let id = createdIds.get(target.name);
522:           if (id === undefined) {
523:             throw new Error(`Agent spawner binding "${bindingName}" references binding ` +
524:                 `"${target.name}", which was not assigned.`);
525:           }
526:           env[envName] = id;
527:         }
528:       }
529: 
530:       let config: AgentSpawnerConfig = {
531:         displayName: blueprintBinding.title,
532:         modelId: assignment.modelId,
533:         env,
534:       };
535:       using gk = await overseerResult.newAgentSpawnerGatekeeper(config);
536:       await gadget.bind(bindingName, await gk.getId());
537:     }
538: 
539:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
540:       event_name: "gadget_created",
541:       user_id: this.#userId.toString(),
542:       gadget_id: id,
543:       blueprint_id: blueprintId,
544:       source: "blueprint",
545:     });
546: 
547:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC stubs are compatible but the type
548:     //     system doesn't know this.
549:     return overseerResult;
550:   }

797:   /**
798:    * Replace the set of outputs recorded for one workspace. Called by that workspace's Overseer
799:    * whenever its gadget registry changes and whenever it is opened.
800:    *
801:    * A workspace the user no longer tracks (deleted, or a shared one they dismissed) has its
802:    * entries dropped.
803:    */
804:   syncWorkspaceOutputs(workspaceId: string, entries: WorkspaceOutputEntry[]): void {
805:     this.storage.outputs.byWorkspace.delete(workspaceId);
806:     if (!this.storage.gadgets.get(workspaceId)) return;

812:   async listOutputs(): Promise<ListOutputsResult> {
813:     let catchingUp = await this.#backfillOutputs();
814:     return {outputs: this.#readOutputs(), catchingUp};
815:   }
816: 
817:   // Ask the user's pre-existing workspaces to populate the outputs index, once. Workspaces push as
818:   // they change and when opened, so only those predating the index need this.
819:   //
820:   // Sweeps one bounded page and reports whether more remains, rather than sweeping everything: a
821:   // first Outputs load must not wait on every workspace the user has ever created. The caller
822:   // drains the rest, so the list fills in while the page is open.
823:   async #backfillOutputs(): Promise<boolean> {
824:     if (this.storage.outputsBackfilled.get()) return false;
825: 
826:     let startAfter = this.storage.outputsBackfillCursor.get() || undefined;
827:     let cursor = startAfter ?? "";
828:     let targets: string[] = [];
829:     let examined = 0;
830:     for (let gadget of this.storage.gadgets.list({startAfter, limit: OUTPUTS_BACKFILL_PAGE})) {
831:       ++examined;
832:       cursor = gadget.id;
833:       // A shared workspace is mirrored on open, not swept; a half-created one has nothing yet.
834:       if (!gadget.owner && isFullyCreated(gadget)) targets.push(gadget.id);
835:     }
836:     let done = examined < OUTPUTS_BACKFILL_PAGE;
837: 
838:     let ownerId = this.ctx.id.toString();
839:     let overseers = this.ctx.exports.OverseerDurableObject;
840:     let results = await Promise.allSettled(targets.map(id =>
841:         overseers.get(overseers.idFromString(id)).getOutputsForOwnerBackfill(ownerId)));
842: 
843:     let failureCount = 0;
844:     let firstError: unknown;
845:     for (let [index, result] of results.entries()) {
846:       if (result.status === "fulfilled") {
847:         if (result.value) this.syncWorkspaceOutputs(targets[index], result.value);
848:       } else {
849:         if (failureCount === 0) firstError = result.reason;
850:         ++failureCount;
851:       }
852:     }
853: 
854:     if (failureCount > 0) {
855:       logger.warn("failed to backfill outputs for some workspaces", {
856:         event: "outputs.backfill.partial",
857:         failureCount,
858:         error: firstError,
859:       });
860:     }
861: 
862:     // Advance past workspaces that failed, rather than retrying them. The index is self-healing,
863:     // so one missed here reappears the moment it is touched, whereas holding the cursor lets a
864:     // single unwakeable workspace stall the sweep forever.
865:     if (done) {
866:       this.storage.outputsBackfilled.put(true);
867:     } else {
868:       this.storage.outputsBackfillCursor.put(cursor);
869:     }
870: 
871:     // A page where everything failed looks systemic, so stop draining and let the next visit pick
872:     // up from the next page: draining on would be a burst of doomed calls during an outage.
873:     if (failureCount > 0 && failureCount === targets.length) return false;
874:     return !done;
875:   }
876: 
877:   #readOutputs(): OutputSummary[] {
878:     let result: OutputSummary[] = [];
879:     for (let output of this.storage.outputs.list()) {
880:       let workspace = this.storage.gadgets.get(output.workspaceId);
881:       if (!workspace || !isFullyCreated(workspace)) continue;
882:       result.push({
883:         workspaceId: output.workspaceId,
884:         workpieceId: output.workpieceId,
885:         ...(output.output ? {output: output.output} : {}),
886:         title: output.title,
887:         workspaceTitle: workspace.title,
888:         created: output.created,
889:         lastActive: workspace.lastActive,
890:         ...(workspace.owner ? {owner: workspace.owner} : {}),
891:         ...(workspace.role ? {role: workspace.role} : {}),
892:       });
893:     }
894:     result.sort((a, b) => b.lastActive.getTime() - a.lastActive.getTime());
895:     return result;
896:   }

1098:       userId: this.storage.profile.get().id
1099:     };
1100: 
1101:     // Admin-disabled resources/gatekeepers are filtered out here, which also covers the agent (the
1102:     // Overseer's connectable-vendor/resource list is sourced from this method).
1103:     let config = await readAdminConfig(this.env);
1104:     let disabledGatekeeperSet = new Set(config.disabledGatekeepers);
1105: 
1106:     let promises: Promise<GatekeeperVendorInfo | null>[] = [];
1107: 
1108:     for (let [id, vendor] of this.vendors) {
1109:       if (disabledGatekeeperSet.has(id)) {
1110:         continue;  // Whole gatekeeper disabled by admin.
1111:       }
1112:       promises.push((async () => {
1113:         if (filter && !(await checkGatekeeperVendorFilter(vendor, id, filter))) {
1114:           return null;
1115:         }
1116: 
1117:         try {
1118:           let [description, supportedResources] = await Promise.all([
1119:             vendor.describe(),
1120:             vendor.getSupportedResources(options),
1121:           ]);
1122:           let enabledResources =
1123:               filterEnabledResources(config, id, supportedResources);
1124:           if (enabledResources.length == 0) {
1125:             // Every resource for this vendor is disabled (or it advertised none) — hide the vendor.
1126:             return null;
1127:           }
1128: 
1129:           return {id, description, supportedResources: enabledResources};
1130:         } catch (err) {
1131:           logger.warn("failed to load gatekeeper vendor", {
1132:             event: "gatekeeper.vendor.load.failed", vendorId: id, error: err,
1133:           });
1134:           return unavailableGatekeeperVendorInfo(id);
1135:         }
1136:       })());
1137:     }
1138: 
1139:     return (await Promise.all(promises)).filter(value => value !== null);
1140:   }

1142:   async connectAccount(vendorId: string, resourceUrlPatterns?: string[]): Promise<{url: string}> {
1143:     let vendor = this.vendors.get(vendorId);
1144:     if (!vendor) {
1145:       throw new Error("No such service: " + vendorId);
1146:     }
1147:     if ((await readAdminConfig(this.env)).disabledGatekeepers.includes(vendorId.toLowerCase())) {
1148:       throw new Error(`The "${vendorId}" gatekeeper is disabled on this deployment.`);
1149:     }
1150: 
1151:     let accountId = this.storage.nextAccountId.get();
1152:     this.storage.nextAccountId.put(accountId + 1);
1153: 
1154:     let props = {
1155:       userId: this.ctx.id.toString(),
1156:       accountId,
1157:       vendorId,
1158:     };
1159: 
1160:     let callback = this.ctx.exports.GatekeeperConnectCallbackImpl({props});
1161: 
1162:     let {url} = await vendor.connectAccount(callback, {resourceUrlPatterns});
1163:     logger.info("account connect started", {
1164:       event: "account.connect.started", vendorId, accountId,
1165:     });
1166:     return {url};
1167:   }
1168: 
1169:   // Iterate every connected-account record, skipping any that fails to load. A record can fail to
1170:   // deserialize when its account stub points at a gatekeeper Worker that's no longer bound in this
1171:   // deployment (workerd throws "Stub refers to a service that doesn't exist"). Skipping it keeps one
1172:   // stale account from breaking listing, provisioning, and opt-in for all the others — the same
1173:   // resilience subscribeConnectedAccounts relies on (it iterates through this).
1174:   *#connectedAccountRecords(): Generator<ConnectedAccountRecord> {
1175:     let nextAccountId = this.storage.nextAccountId.get();
1176:     for (let id = 0; id < nextAccountId; id++) {
1177:       let rec: ConnectedAccountRecord | undefined;
1178:       try {
1179:         rec = this.storage.connectedAccounts.get(id);
1180:       } catch (err) {
1181:         logger.warn("skipping connected account: failed to load", {
1182:           event: "connected.account.load.skipped", accountId: id, error: err,
1183:         });
1184:         continue;
1185:       }
1186:       if (rec) yield rec;
1187:     }
1188:   }

1190:   // Whether this user already has a connected account for the given vendor.
1191:   #hasAccountForVendor(vendorId: string): boolean {
1192:     for (let rec of this.#connectedAccountRecords()) {
1193:       if (rec.vendorId === vendorId) return true;
1194:     }
1195:     return false;
1196:   }

1198:   // Resolve every bound vendor that auto-provisions an account (VendorDescription.autoProvisionsAccount),
1199:   // describing them in parallel and dropping any whose describe() fails. Shared discovery step for both
1200:   // listing and auto-provisioning ambient gatekeepers; callers apply their own admin-mode filter.
1201:   async #ambientVendors():
1202:       Promise<Array<{vendorId: string, vendor: Service<GatekeeperVendor>, description: VendorDescription}>> {
1203:     let described = await Promise.all([...this.vendors].map(async ([vendorId, vendor]) => {
1204:       try {
1205:         let description = await vendor.describe();
1206:         return description.autoProvisionsAccount ? {vendorId, vendor, description} : null;
1207:       } catch (err) {
1208:         logger.warn("failed to describe vendor", {
1209:           event: "vendor.describe.failed", vendorId, error: err,
1210:         });
1211:         return null;
1212:       }
1213:     }));
1214:     return described.filter(v => v !== null);
1215:   }

1217:   /**
1218:    * The ambient gatekeepers the user can opt into now: mode "optional" and not yet added. Backs the
1219:    * Connectors "Available" section. ("enabled" ones are already provisioned; "disabled" ones aren't
1220:    * offered.)
1221:    */
1222:   async listAddableGatekeepers(): Promise<GatekeeperVendorInfo[]> {
1223:     let config = await readAdminConfig(this.env);
1224:     return (await this.#ambientVendors())
1225:         .filter(({vendorId}) =>
1226:             ambientGatekeeperMode(config, vendorId) === "optional" && !this.#hasAccountForVendor(vendorId))
1227:         // Same shape as listGatekeeperVendors; ambient gatekeepers expose no resources.
1228:         .map(({vendorId, description}) => ({id: vendorId, description, supportedResources: []}));
1229:   }

1231:   // Per-vendor dedup of concurrent provisionAmbientAccount() calls — same DO-input-gate race as
1232:   // #ensureAccountsPromise (see its comment below), e.g. a double-click on "Add". Cleared on completion.
1233:   #provisionPromises = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
1234: 
1235:   /**
1236:    * Opt into an ambient gatekeeper on demand: mint its connected account for this user (no OAuth).
1237:    * Only when the vendor's mode isn't "disabled" and the user has no account yet. Idempotent.
1238:    */
1239:   provisionAmbientAccount(vendorId: string): Promise<void> {
1240:     vendorId = vendorId.toLowerCase();
1241:     let inFlight = this.#provisionPromises.get(vendorId);
1242:     if (inFlight) return inFlight;
1243:     let promise = this.#provisionAmbientAccount(vendorId)
1244:         .finally(() => { this.#provisionPromises.delete(vendorId); });
1245:     this.#provisionPromises.set(vendorId, promise);
1246:     return promise;
1247:   }

1249:   async #provisionAmbientAccount(vendorId: string): Promise<void> {
1250:     let vendor = this.vendors.get(vendorId);
1251:     if (!vendor) throw new Error("No such service: " + vendorId);
1252: 
1253:     if (ambientGatekeeperMode(await readAdminConfig(this.env), vendorId) === "disabled") {
1254:       throw new Error(`The "${vendorId}" gatekeeper is disabled on this deployment.`);
1255:     }
1256: 
1257:     let description = await vendor.describe();
1258:     if (!description.autoProvisionsAccount) {
1259:       throw new Error(`The "${vendorId}" gatekeeper can't be added this way.`);
1260:     }
1261: 
1262:     if (this.#hasAccountForVendor(vendorId)) return;  // already added
1263: 
1264:     await this.#createAutoProvisionedAccount(vendorId, vendor);
1265:   }
1266: 
1267:   // Mint a vendor's connected account with no OAuth flow and persist it as auto-provisioned. The
1268:   // caller must have already confirmed the vendor sets autoProvisionsAccount (so createAccount is
1269:   // present) and that the user has no account for it yet.
1270:   async #createAutoProvisionedAccount(vendorId: string, vendor: Service<GatekeeperVendor>): Promise<void> {
1271:     let account = await (vendor as unknown as AccountCreatorStub).createAccount();
1272:     // Resolve the description before allocating the id, so a describe() failure doesn't burn a slot.
1273:     let description = await account.describe();
1274:     let accountId = this.storage.nextAccountId.get();
1275:     this.storage.nextAccountId.put(accountId + 1);
1276:     this.storage.connectedAccounts.put({
1277:       id: accountId,
1278:       account,
1279:       description,
1280:       vendorId,
1281:       autoProvisioned: true,
1282:     });
1283:   }
1284: 
1285:   // Dedup concurrent #ensureAutoProvisionedAccounts() calls. The provisioning loop awaits cross-worker
1286:   // RPCs (describe/createAccount), which releases the DO input gate; without this, two overlapping
1287:   // calls (e.g. the nav listing apps while a gadget opens) could both see "not provisioned" and
1288:   // create duplicate accounts. Cleared on completion so a later call re-checks (e.g. for a gatekeeper
1289:   // bound after this DO started).
1290:   #ensureAccountsPromise?: Promise<void>;
1291:

19: function makeAdminSettingsStorage(storage: DurableObjectStorage) {
20:   return createTypedStorage(storage, {
21:     collections: {
22:       // Mirror of the currently-featured blueprint public records. The user DO owns the
23:       // authoritative featured bit; this DO keeps the publishable deployment-wide copy.
24:       featuredBlueprints: collection<BlueprintPublicInfo>()({
25:         primaryKey: 'id',
26:       }),
27:     },
28:     singletons: {
29:       // Authoritative deployment admin config. Mirrored to BLUEPRINTS KV (ADMIN_CONFIG_KEY) so the
30:       // connect/login/agent hot paths can read it without touching this singleton DO.
31:       adminConfig: DEFAULT_ADMIN_CONFIG as AdminConfig,
32: 
33:       // Which set of bundled format blueprints has been installed (see
34:       // formatBlueprintsManifestVersion). Empty means none yet; a mismatch means the repo shipped
35:       // new or updated ones and they should be reinstalled.
36:       installedFormatBlueprints: "",
37: 
38:       // Bundled blueprint ids that have already been offered for promotion into
39:       // AdminConfig.formats. Tracked separately from the install stamp so that promotion happens
40:       // exactly once per blueprint: an admin who then removes a format keeps it removed, while a
41:       // deployment that installed before curation existed still gets promoted.
42:       promotedFormatBlueprints: <string[]>[],
43:     },
44:   });
45: }
46: 
47: type AdminSettingsStorage = ReturnType<typeof makeAdminSettingsStorage>;
48: 
49: /**
50:  * Deployment-wide admin settings singleton.
51:  *
52:  * This durable object is always addressed as `getByName("")`. It contains settings that only
53:  * admins may modify. Settings modified through this DO are published to KV so that user requests
54:  * do not have to access the AdminSettings DO directly (which they could otherwise overload), but
55:  * having a singleton DO writing to KV avoids race conditions when updating KV.
56:  */
57: export class AdminSettings extends DurableObject<Cloudflare.Env> {
58:   private storage: AdminSettingsStorage;
59:   private users: DurableObjectNamespace<UserDurableObject>;
60:   // Every bound gatekeeper, keyed by vendor id. Deployment-global (from env bindings), so admin
61:   // resource listing needs no user context.
62:   private vendors: Map<string, Service<GatekeeperVendor>>;
63:   // Every config setter writes the same authoritative singleton and KV mirror. Serialize the full
64:   // read/modify/write operation so external KV I/O cannot let concurrent setters lose updates.
65:   private adminConfigMutationTail = Promise.resolve();
66:   // R2 and config are separate stores. Serialize logo changes so reset/upload operations cannot
67:   // interleave while switching whether the fixed public object is enabled.
68:   private siteLogoMutationTail = Promise.resolve();
69: 
70:   constructor(ctx: DurableObjectState, env: Cloudflare.Env) {
71:     super(ctx, env);
72: 
73:     this.storage = makeAdminSettingsStorage(ctx.storage);
74:     this.users = this.ctx.exports.UserDurableObject;
75:     this.vendors = buildGatekeeperVendorMap(env);
76:   }

78:   /**
79:    * Install the format blueprints bundled with this deployment, if that hasn't already happened
80:    * for this exact manifest. Idempotent and cheap: an up-to-date deployment does one string
81:    * comparison and returns.
82:    *
83:    * Written straight into the featured mirror rather than through setBlueprintFeatured(), whose
84:    * authoritative bit lives in the publishing user's DO -- these have no owning user.
85:    *
86:    * Callers are coalesced onto one run, or two isolates racing on a fresh deployment both promote
87:    * the same blueprints, and a duplicated id makes setFormatOrder() reject every reordering.
88:    */
89:   ensureFormatBlueprintsInstalled(): Promise<boolean> {
90:     return this.#installInFlight ??= this.#installFormatBlueprints()
91:         .finally(() => { this.#installInFlight = undefined; });
92:   }
93: 
94:   #installInFlight?: Promise<boolean>;
95: 
96:   // Resolves true once every bundled blueprint is live. A partial install resolves false rather
97:   // than throwing: the caller has nothing to handle, but it does need to know to ask again.
98:   async #installFormatBlueprints(): Promise<boolean> {
99:     let complete = true;
100:     let manifestVersion = formatBlueprintsManifestVersion();
101:     if (this.storage.installedFormatBlueprints.get() !== manifestVersion) {
102:       let installed = await installFormatBlueprints(this.env);
103: 
104:       if (installed.length > 0) {
105:         for (let publicInfo of installed) {
106:           this.storage.featuredBlueprints.put(publicInfo);
107:         }
108:         await this.#writeFeaturedSnapshot();
109:       }
110: 
111:       // Stamped only once the whole manifest is live, so a crash or a single bad archive retries
112:       // next time. Recording a partial install as complete would strand the entries that failed
113:       // until the manifest happened to change again.
114:       complete = installed.length === FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.length;
115:       if (complete) {
116:         this.storage.installedFormatBlueprints.put(manifestVersion);
117:       }
118:       logger.info("installed bundled format blueprints", {
119:         event: "formats.install.complete",
120:         size: installed.length,
121:         failureCount: FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.length - installed.length,
122:       });
123:     }
124: 
125:     // Promotion is checked on every run, not just after an install, so a deployment that installed
126:     // before curation existed still ends up offering its bundled formats.
127:     await this.#promoteBundledFormats();
128:     return complete;
129:   }
130: 
131:   // Offer each bundled blueprint as a standard format, once ever. A separate one-shot decision per
132:   // blueprint: re-deriving the list from the manifest would undo an admin's removal on every
133:   // startup, and reinstalling an updated archive must refresh the blueprint without resetting how
134:   // the deployment has chosen to offer it.
135:   //
136:   // The converse isn't handled: a blueprint dropped from the bundle, or given a new blueprintId,
137:   // leaves its record and its promotion behind for an admin to remove by hand. Withdrawing them
138:   // would mean tracking which promotions this installer made, which is worth doing before the
139:   // bundled set ever changes.
140:   async #promoteBundledFormats(): Promise<void> {
141:     let promoted = new Set(this.storage.promotedFormatBlueprints.get());
142:     let pending = FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.filter(entry => !promoted.has(entry.blueprintId));
143:     if (pending.length === 0) return;
144: 
145:     let config = this.#config();
146:     let known = new Set(config.formats.map(f => f.blueprintId));
147:     let added = pending
148:         .filter(entry => !known.has(entry.blueprintId))
149:         .map(entry => ({blueprintId: entry.blueprintId, enabled: true}));
150:     // Always write, even when every pending format is already in DO storage. That is the retry
151:     // state after a prior KV mirror failure; stamping promotion without writing would strand the
152:     // hot-path mirror on its old config forever.
153:     await this.updateAdminConfig({formats: [...config.formats, ...added]});
154: 
155:     for (let entry of pending) promoted.add(entry.blueprintId);
156:     this.storage.promotedFormatBlueprints.put([...promoted]);
157:   }

159:   async #writeFeaturedSnapshot(): Promise<void> {
160:     let featured = [...this.storage.featuredBlueprints.list()];
161:     await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.put(FEATURED_BLUEPRINTS_KEY, serializeFeaturedBlueprints(featured));
162:   }

164:   // Reconcile the mirrored featured list to match the authoritative bit stored in the owner
165:   // User DO, while also refreshing stale metadata snapshots for featured entries.
166:   async #syncFeaturedMirror(publicInfo: BlueprintPublicInfo, featured: boolean): Promise<void> {
167:     let existing = this.storage.featuredBlueprints.get(publicInfo.id);
168:     let changed = false;
169: 
170:     if (!featured) {
171:       if (existing) {
172:         this.storage.featuredBlueprints.delete(publicInfo.id);
173:         changed = true;
174:       }
175:     } else if (
176:       !existing ||
177:       existing.metadata.version !== publicInfo.metadata.version ||
178:       existing.metadata.lastUpdated.valueOf() !== publicInfo.metadata.lastUpdated.valueOf()
179:     ) {
180:       this.storage.featuredBlueprints.put(publicInfo);
181:       changed = true;
182:     }
183: 
184:     if (changed) {
185:       await this.#writeFeaturedSnapshot();
186:     }
187:   }

189:   async #getOwnerBlueprint(blueprintId: string): Promise<{
190:     // Absent for a blueprint with no owning user, in which case `featureable` is false.
191:     owner: DurableObjectStub<UserDurableObject> | undefined;
192:     publicInfo: BlueprintPublicInfo;
193:     featureable: boolean;
194:   }> {
195:     if (isReservedBlueprintKey(blueprintId)) {
196:       throw new Error('Blueprint not found.');
197:     }
198: 
199:     let raw = await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.get(blueprintId);
200:     if (!raw) {
201:       throw new Error('Blueprint not found.');
202:     }
203: 
204:     let kvRecord = parseBlueprintKvRecord(raw);
205: 
206:     return {
207:       owner: kvRecord.ownerId
208:           ? this.users.get(this.users.idFromString(kvRecord.ownerId))
209:           : undefined,
210:       publicInfo: {
211:         id: blueprintId,
212:         metadata: kvRecord.metadata,
213:       },
214:       // A deployment-installed blueprint (see format-blueprints.ts) has no owning User DO to hold
215:       // the authoritative featured bit, so the owner-anchored toggle doesn't apply -- the same
216:       // answer as an uploaded blueprint. It reaches users through the deployment's curation.
217:       featureable: !!kvRecord.gadgetId && !!kvRecord.ownerId,
218:     };
219:   }

221:   async isBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId: string): Promise<boolean | null> {
222:     let { owner, publicInfo, featureable } = await this.#getOwnerBlueprint(blueprintId);
223:     if (!featureable || !owner) {
224:       return null;
225:     }
226: 
227:     let featured = await owner.isBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId);
228:     if (featured === null) {
229:       return null;
230:     }
231: 
232:     // Heal partial failures before answering so admin reads never observe disagreement.
233:     await this.#syncFeaturedMirror(publicInfo, featured);
234:     return featured;
235:   }
236: 
237:   async setBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId: string, featured: boolean): Promise<void> {
238:     let { owner, publicInfo, featureable } = await this.#getOwnerBlueprint(blueprintId);
239:     if (!featureable || !owner) {
240:       throw new Error('Blueprint not featureable.');
241:     }
242: 
243:     await owner.setBlueprintFeatured(blueprintId, featured);
244:     await this.#syncFeaturedMirror(publicInfo, featured);
245:   }

247:   async syncFeaturedBlueprint(publicInfo: BlueprintPublicInfo): Promise<void> {
248:     // Overseer propagation calls this after blueprint updates so the mirror keeps up with the
249:     // latest published metadata, but only while the owner-side featured bit stays enabled.
250:     await this.#syncFeaturedMirror(publicInfo, true);
251:   }

253:   async deleteFeaturedBlueprint(blueprintId: string): Promise<void> {

260:   // --- Deployment admin config ---
261: 
262:   // Every read of the stored config goes through here. A config persisted before a field existed
263:   // is missing that field entirely, so reads must backfill from the defaults or the first
264:   // deployment to upgrade hits `undefined` on it.
265:   #config(): AdminConfig {
266:     return { ...DEFAULT_ADMIN_CONFIG, ...this.storage.adminConfig.get() };

273:   async #mutateAdminConfig(mutate: (config: AdminConfig) => AdminConfig): Promise<void> {
274:     let previousMutation = this.adminConfigMutationTail;
275:     let release!: () => void;
276:     this.adminConfigMutationTail = new Promise<void>(resolve => { release = resolve; });
277:     await previousMutation;
278:     try {
279:       let current = this.#config();
280:       let next = mutate(current);
281:       this.storage.adminConfig.put(next);
282:       try {
283:         await this.env.BLUEPRINTS.put(ADMIN_CONFIG_KEY, serializeAdminConfig(next));
284:       } catch (error) {
285:         this.storage.adminConfig.put(current);
286:         throw error;
287:       }
288:     } finally {
289:       release();
290:     }
291:   }

302:    * Read all admin-managed settings for the admin UI in one call: the stored config plus the live

305:    * `adminUserId` is the requesting admin's user id (email/username), forwarded to each gatekeeper's

327:   // Admin view of the promoted formats: the deployment's curation joined with each blueprint, so
328:   // the panel can show what is being curated and flag entries whose blueprint has been deleted.
329:   async #listFormatConfig(config: AdminConfig): Promise<AdminFormat[]> {
330:     let bundled = new Set(FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.map(entry => entry.blueprintId));
331: 
332:     // Every entry, not just the offered ones: the panel exists to show what is disabled and what
333:     // points at a deleted blueprint.
334:     return (await listPromotedFormats(this.env, config.formats)).map(
335:         ({entry, metadata, declared, output}) => ({
336:           blueprintId: entry.blueprintId,
337:           blueprintTitle: metadata?.title ?? "",
338:           blueprintDescription: metadata?.description ?? "",
339:           output,
340:           declared,
341:           overrides: entry.overrides,
342:           enabled: entry.enabled,
343:           agentHint: entry.agentHint ?? "",
344:           missing: !metadata,
345:           bundled: bundled.has(entry.blueprintId),
346:         }));
347:   }

349:   // Read-modify-write one format entry within the DO, so concurrent admin edits can't clobber each
350:   // other. `mutate` returns the replacement list, or null to leave the config untouched.
351:   async #mutateFormats(mutate: (formats: FormatCuration[]) => FormatCuration[] | null)
352:       : Promise<void> {
353:     await this.#mutateAdminConfig(config => {
354:       let next = mutate(config.formats);
355:       // A no-op may be a retry after the prior KV write failed but DO storage succeeded. Mirror the
356:       // current config again so idempotent retries repair that partial failure.
357:       return next ? {...config, formats: next} : config;
358:     });
359:   }

361:   async promoteFormat(blueprintId: string): Promise<void> {
362:     let record = await readBlueprintKvRecord(this.env, blueprintId);
363:     if (!record) {
364:       throw new Error("Blueprint not found.");
365:     }
366:     await this.#mutateFormats(formats => {
367:       // Idempotent so retrying after a KV mirror failure reaches #mutateFormats()'s repair write.
368:       if (formats.some(f => f.blueprintId === blueprintId)) return null;
369:       // A blueprint that declares no output still needs a stable grouping key before the admin can
370:       // name it. Generate that hidden implementation detail here; the panel only asks the admin for
371:       // the human-facing noun, plural and icon.
372:       let declared = sanitizeBlueprintOutput(record.metadata.output);
373:       return [...formats, {
374:         blueprintId,
375:         enabled: true,
376:         ...(declared ? {} : {overrides: {id: defaultOutputFormatId(blueprintId)}}),
377:       }];
378:     });
379:   }

381:   async removeFormat(blueprintId: string): Promise<void> {
382:     // Enforced here, not just in the panel: this is an RPC an admin session can call directly.
383:     // Withdrawing a bundled entry is `enabled: false`, which keeps its overrides, hint and
384:     // position.
385:     if (FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS.some(entry => entry.blueprintId === blueprintId)) {
386:       throw new Error(
387:           "This format ships with the deployment, so it can't be removed. Turn it off instead.");
388:     }
389:     await this.#mutateFormats(formats => {
390:       let next = formats.filter(f => f.blueprintId !== blueprintId);
391:       return next.length === formats.length ? null : next;
392:     });
393:   }

395:   async updateFormat(blueprintId: string, patch: AdminFormatPatch): Promise<void> {
396:     await this.#mutateFormats(formats => formats.map(entry => {
397:       if (entry.blueprintId !== blueprintId) return entry;
398: 
399:       let next: FormatCuration = {...entry};
400:       if (patch.enabled !== undefined) next.enabled = patch.enabled;
401:       if (patch.agentHint !== undefined) {
402:         // Truncated because every hint is repeated in the system prompt on every turn, so an
403:         // over-long one costs tokens on requests nobody connects back to this panel.
404:         let hint = patch.agentHint.trim().slice(0, MAX_AGENT_HINT);
405:         if (hint) next.agentHint = hint; else delete next.agentHint;
406:       }
407:       if (patch.overrides) {
408:         // null reverts a field to the blueprint's own declaration; absent leaves it alone.
409:         let merged: Record<string, unknown> = {...entry.overrides};
410:         for (let [key, value] of Object.entries(patch.overrides)) {
411:           if (value === null) delete merged[key]; else merged[key] = value;
412:         }
413:         let clean = sanitizeOutputOverrides(merged);
414:         if (clean) next.overrides = clean; else delete next.overrides;
415:       }
416:       return next;
417:     }));
418:   }

467:   /**
468:    * Set a gatekeeper's availability atomically (read-modify-write within the DO). Routes by kind: an
469:    * auto-provisioning ("ambient") gatekeeper stores its three-state mode in ambientGatekeeperModes
470:    * (default stored as absence); an ordinary gatekeeper stores a binary enabled/disabled in
471:    * disabledGatekeepers and rejects the ambient-only 'optional'.
472:    */
473:   async setGatekeeperMode(vendorId: string, mode: AmbientGatekeeperMode): Promise<void> {
474:     vendorId = vendorId.toLowerCase();
475:     let vendor = this.vendors.get(vendorId);
476:     let autoProvisions = !!vendor && (await vendor.describe()).autoProvisionsAccount === true;
477:     if (autoProvisions) {
478:       await this.#mutateAdminConfig(config => {
479:         let modes = { ...config.ambientGatekeeperModes };
480:         if (mode === DEFAULT_AMBIENT_GATEKEEPER_MODE) delete modes[vendorId]; else modes[vendorId] = mode;
481:         return { ...config, ambientGatekeeperModes: modes };
482:       });
483:     } else {
484:       if (mode === "optional") {
485:         throw new Error(`"${vendorId}" is not an auto-provisioning gatekeeper; use 'enabled' or 'disabled'.`);
486:       }
487:       await this.#mutateAdminConfig(config => {
488:         let disabled = new Set(config.disabledGatekeepers);
489:         if (mode === "enabled") disabled.delete(vendorId); else disabled.add(vendorId);
490:         return { ...config, disabledGatekeepers: [...disabled] };
491:       });
492:     }
493:   }

495:   // Admin view of every bound gatekeeper's resource types, annotated with their enabled state.
496:   // Unlike the user-facing listGatekeeperVendors, this does NOT hide disabled resources (so admins
497:   // can re-enable them). `adminUserId` is forwarded to getSupportedResources() so RBAC-gated
498:   // gatekeepers still surface for an admin who has access to them.
499:   async #listResourceConfig(config: AdminConfig, adminUserId: string): Promise<AdminResourceVendor[]> {
500:     let disabledGatekeeperSet = new Set(config.disabledGatekeepers);
501: 
502:     let promises: Promise<AdminResourceVendor | null>[] = [];
503:     for (let [id, vendor] of this.vendors) {
504:       promises.push((async () => {
505:         try {
506:           let [description, supportedResources] = await Promise.all([
507:             vendor.describe(),
508:             vendor.getSupportedResources({ userId: adminUserId }),
509:           ]);
510:           if (description.autoProvisionsAccount) {
511:             // Auto-provisioning ("ambient") gatekeeper: a three-state mode, no resources to toggle.
512:             let mode = ambientGatekeeperMode(config, id);
513:             return {
514:               vendorId: id,
515:               displayName: description.displayName,
516:               logo: description.logo,
517:               autoProvisions: true,
518:               ambientMode: mode,
519:             };
520:           }
521:           if (supportedResources.length === 0) {
522:             // Nothing to toggle for this gatekeeper.
523:             return null;
524:           }
525:           let disabled = new Set(config.disabledResources[id] ?? []);
526:           return {
527:             vendorId: id,
528:             displayName: description.displayName,
529:             logo: description.logo,
530:             autoProvisions: false,
531:             enabled: !disabledGatekeeperSet.has(id),
532:             resources: supportedResources.map(r => ({
533:               urlPattern: r.urlPattern,
534:               title: r.title,
535:               description: r.description,
536:               icon: r.icon,
537:               enabled: !disabled.has(r.urlPattern),
538:             })),
539:           };
540:         } catch (err) {
541:           logger.warn("failed to read resource config for gatekeeper", {
542:             event: "gatekeeper.resource.config.read.failed", gatekeeperId: id, error: err,
543:           });
544:           return null;
545:         }
546:       })());
547:     }
548: 
549:     let vendors = (await Promise.all(promises)).filter((v): v is AdminResourceVendor => v !== null);
550:     // Show auto-provisioned ("ambient") gatekeepers first; preserve the existing order otherwise.
551:     vendors.sort((a, b) => Number(b.autoProvisions) - Number(a.autoProvisions));
552:     return vendors;
553:   }
554: }

1: // Usage checker: combines the daily free-tier counter with the BYOK/balance logic to decide
2: // whether a user's request may proceed, and whose credentials to use.
3: //
4: // Billing rules (see canProceedWithRequest):
5: //   - Connected + balance >= minimum -> billed to the user's own gateway, no daily cap; the daily
6: //     counter is NOT consumed (the platform free tier is reserved for everyone else).
7: //   - Connected + balance below minimum (incl. $0), or not connected -> platform free tier; the
8: //     daily counter is consumed and, once exhausted, the request is blocked.
9: 
10: import { canProceedWithRequest, hasMinimumBalance, LimitWindowKind } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/limits";
11: import { CloudflareUsageInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
12: import { isCloudflareLimitsEnabled, getMinimumCloudflareBalance } from "../config.js";
13: import { getDailyLlmCallLimit } from "./config.js";
14: import { getConnectionStatus, resolveConnection, ByokGatewayRouting } from "../cloudflare/connection-service.js";
15: import type { UserDurableObject } from "../../user.js";
16: 
17: export interface UsageCheckResult {
18:   /** Whether the request may proceed. */
19:   allowed: boolean;
20:   /** Guidance/reason when blocked. */
21:   reason?: string;
22:   /** Whether to serve the request using the user's own gateway/keys rather than the platform's. */
23:   shouldUseByok: boolean;
24:   /** Whether the user is within their free-tier limit. */
25:   withinLimits: boolean;
26:   /** Calls remaining in the current window (Infinity when limits are disabled). */
27:   remaining: number;
28:   /** The configured limit (Infinity when limits are disabled). */
29:   limit: number;
30:   /** Window kind and reset time (omitted when unlimited). */
31:   windowKind?: LimitWindowKind;
32:   resetAt?: string;
33:   /** The user's Cloudflare AI Gateway balance, or null if unknown / not connected. */
34:   balance: number | null;
35:   /** Whether the user has connected a Cloudflare account with a usable token. */
36:   hasUserToken: boolean;
37:   /**
38:    * Routing to bill the user's own account, present only when shouldUseByok is true. Resolved here
39:    * (reusing the connection lookup) so the caller needn't decrypt the token a second time.
40:    */
41:   byokRouting?: ByokGatewayRouting;
42: }
43: 
44: // Result used when limits are disabled (self-hosted / unlimited).
45: function unlimitedResult(): UsageCheckResult {
46:   return {
47:     allowed: true,
48:     shouldUseByok: false,
49:     withinLimits: true,
50:     remaining: Infinity,
51:     limit: Infinity,
52:     balance: null,
53:     hasUserToken: false,
54:   };
55: }
56: 
57: /**
58:  * Check whether the user may proceed with an LLM-backed request.
59:  *
60:  * When limits are disabled, always allows without touching the user object. Otherwise: connected +
61:  * funded users bill their own gateway and skip the daily counter entirely; everyone else draws on
62:  * the platform free tier (consuming one call against the user object) until it's exhausted.
63:  */
64: export async function checkUsageAndBalance(
65:   env: Cloudflare.Env,
66:   userStub: DurableObjectStub<UserDurableObject>,
67: ): Promise<UsageCheckResult> {
68:   if (!isCloudflareLimitsEnabled(env)) {
69:     return unlimitedResult();
70:   }
71: 
72:   const limit = getDailyLlmCallLimit(env);
73:   const minimumBalance = getMinimumCloudflareBalance(env);
74: 
75:   // Resolve the connected-account status up front: it determines billing even within the free tier
76:   // (connected + funded users always bill their own gateway). `balance` is null when not connected
77:   // or when the balance can't be read — treated as "not funded" so we fall back to the free tier
78:   // rather than attempting a BYOK call that would fail.
79:   let hasUserToken = false;
80:   let balance: number | null = null;
81:   // Routing to bill the user's own account, derivable only when connected with a resolved account.
82:   let byokRouting: ByokGatewayRouting | undefined;
83:   const conn = await resolveConnection(env, userStub);
84:   hasUserToken = conn.status.connected;
85:   balance = conn.status.balance;
86:   if (conn.accessToken && conn.accountId) {
87:     byokRouting = { accountId: conn.accountId, apiKey: conn.accessToken };
88:   }
89: 
90:   // Connected + funded -> bill their gateway; don't touch the daily free-tier counter.
91:   if (hasUserToken && hasMinimumBalance(balance, minimumBalance)) {
92:     return {
93:       allowed: true,
94:       shouldUseByok: true,
95:       withinLimits: true,
96:       remaining: Infinity,
97:       limit: Infinity,
98:       balance,
99:       hasUserToken,
100:       byokRouting,
101:     };
102:   }
103: 
104:   // Otherwise draw on the platform free tier. consumeDailyLlmCall() only increments while within

141:       dailyLimit: 0,
142:       remaining: 0,

146:   }

150:   const [quota, status] = await Promise.all([

152:     getConnectionStatus(env, userStub),
153:   ]);

155:   return {
156:     cloudflareLimitsEnabled: true,
157:     unlimited: false,
158:     dailyUsed: quota.used,
159:     dailyLimit: quota.limit,
160:     remaining: quota.remaining,
161:     resetAt: quota.resetAt,
162:     connected: status.connected,
163:     balance: status.balance,

168: }

1: // Thin client over the Cloudflare REST API used by the top-up flow: enumerate the user's accounts
2: // and read the account's AI Gateway credit balance.
3: //
4: // All calls use the user's OAuth access token (obtained via the connect flow).
5: //
6: // Note: connected-user inference is routed through the account's auto-created "default" AI Gateway
7: // (see ai-models.ts), billed via Unified Billing. We only ever need the account id here — no gateway
8: // is listed or chosen.
9: 
10: import { createWorkshopLogger } from "../../observability";
11: 
12: const API_BASE = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4";
13: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.ai.gateway.billing");
14: 
15: interface CfEnvelope<T> {
16:   success: boolean;
17:   result?: T;
18:   result_info?: { per_page?: number; total_count?: number };
19: }
20: 
21: export interface CloudflareAccount {
22:   accountId: string;
23:   accountName: string;
24: }
25: 
26: async function cfRequest<T>(token: string, path: string): Promise<CfEnvelope<T> | null> {
27:   const resp = await fetch(`${API_BASE}${path}`, {
28:     headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
29:   });
30:   if (!resp.ok) {
31:     logger.error("cf-account GET failed", {
32:       event: "cloudflare.account.get.failed",
33:       path, status: resp.status, statusText: resp.statusText,
34:     });
35:     return null;
36:   }
37:   const data = await resp.json() as CfEnvelope<T>;
38:   if (!data.success || data.result === undefined) return null;
39:   return data;
40: }
41: 
42: async function cfGet<T>(token: string, path: string): Promise<T | null> {
43:   return (await cfRequest<T>(token, path))?.result ?? null;
44: }
45: 
46: // `/accounts` is paginated and defaults to 20 per page, so an unpaginated GET hides every account
47: // after the first 20 and the user cannot pick one of them to bill.
48: const ACCOUNTS_PER_PAGE = 50;
49: // Bounds the walk at 500 accounts, since the loop is driven by the provider's own paging.
50: const MAX_ACCOUNT_PAGES = 10;
51: 
52: /** List every account the token can access. Requires the `account-settings.read` OAuth scope. */
53: export async function listAccounts(token: string): Promise<CloudflareAccount[]> {
54:   let accounts: CloudflareAccount[] = [];
55:   for (let page = 1; page <= MAX_ACCOUNT_PAGES; page++) {
56:     let query = new URLSearchParams({
57:       page: String(page),
58:       per_page: String(ACCOUNTS_PER_PAGE),
59:     });
60:     let envelope = await cfRequest<Array<{ id: string; name: string }>>(
61:       token, `/accounts?${query}`,
62:     );
63:     // A page that fails mid-walk yields what was gathered: a partial list beats none, and cfRequest
64:     // has already logged the failure.
65:     if (!envelope?.result) break;
66:     let result = envelope.result;
67:     accounts.push(...result.map((a) => ({ accountId: a.id, accountName: a.name })));
68:     let perPage = envelope.result_info?.per_page ?? ACCOUNTS_PER_PAGE;
69:     if (result.length < perPage) break;
70:     let total = envelope.result_info?.total_count;
71:     if (total !== undefined && accounts.length >= total) break;
72:   }
73:   return accounts;
74: }
75: 
76: /**
77:  * Fetch the account's AI Gateway credit balance in USD. Returns null on any upstream failure so
78:  * callers can distinguish "unknown" from a genuine $0 balance.
79:  */
80: export async function fetchCreditBalance(token: string, accountId: string): Promise<number | null> {
81:   const result = await cfGet<{ balance?: number }>(
82:     token, `/accounts/${accountId}/ai-gateway-billing/credit_balance`,
83:   );
84:   if (!result || typeof result.balance !== "number") return null;
85:   // The API reports the balance in cents.
86:   return result.balance / 100;

10: 
11: import { listAccounts, fetchCreditBalance } from "./account-service.js";
12: import type { UserDurableObject } from "../../user.js";

19: /** Public-safe connection status for display and for the usage decision. */
20: export interface CloudflareConnectionStatus {

22:   accountId?: string;
23:   accountName?: string;
24:   balance: number | null;
25:   /**
26:    * True when connected but the grant sees multiple Cloudflare accounts and none is chosen yet.
27:    * The client must prompt the user to select one via selectAccount().
28:    */
29:   needsAccountSelection?: boolean;
30: }

35:   accountName: string;
36: }

38: /**
39:  * Routing details to bill a user's own Cloudflare account for inference (BYOK path once the free
40:  * tier is spent). Inference is routed through the account's "default" AI Gateway.
41:  */
42: export interface ByokGatewayRouting {
43:   accountId: string;
44:   /** The user's Cloudflare access token, used as the authorization. */
45:   apiKey: string;
46: }

48: /**
49:  * Connection resolution result. `accessToken`/`accountId` are present only when connected with a
50:  * resolved account; `accessToken` is sensitive (never send it to the client).
51:  */
52: export interface ResolvedConnection {
53:   status: CloudflareConnectionStatus;
54:   accessToken?: string;
55:   accountId?: string;
56: }

58: // Get a usable access token from the connected Cloudflare gatekeeper account, or null if the user
59: // hasn't connected Cloudflare or the connection is broken/expired.
60: async function getUsableAccessToken(userStub: UserStub): Promise<string | null> {
61:   // The returned stub is a server-side RPC stub (not an auto-disposed call parameter), so it must be
62:   // disposed to avoid leaking on every call (this runs on the hot path — see resolveConnection).
63:   using account = await userStub.getCloudflareGatekeeperAccount();
64:   if (!account) return null;
65:   return await account.getUsableAccessToken();
66: }

68: /**
69:  * Resolve connection status + balance (cached when fresh), auto-selecting the account when exactly
70:  * one is accessible. Also surfaces the usable access token + resolved account id so a hot-path
71:  * caller can derive BYOK routing without re-reading. Never throws; returns a safe default.
72:  */
73: export async function resolveConnection(
74:   _env: Cloudflare.Env, userStub: UserStub,
75: ): Promise<ResolvedConnection> {
76:   try {
77:     // Dispose the connected-account stub at the end of this call (it's a returned RPC stub, not an
78:     // auto-disposed parameter). This runs on every agent turn and UI refresh.
79:     using account = await userStub.getCloudflareGatekeeperAccount();
80:     if (!account) return { status: { connected: false, balance: null } };
81: 
82:     const accessToken = await account.getUsableAccessToken();
83:     if (!accessToken) {
84:       // Connected, but the token is broken/expired — treat as connected with unknown balance.
85:       return { status: { connected: true, balance: null } };
